summary: Brooke Schedneck specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.
Bror Fredrik Tiliander (1896–1990) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Lund University, was a student of Helmer Smith, and earned his PhD at Uppsala University in 1974.

Bruce B. Lawrence (born 1941) is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Princeton University and Episcopal Divinity School. At Duke University, he served as Professor from circa 1971 to 2012, later becoming Emeritus Professor of Religion.

Bruce Cameron Hall works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Harvard University in 1980 and served as an assistant editor at the College of William & Mary (attested 1987).

Bruce Charles Williams specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.

Bruce Chilton (born 1949) is a religious studies scholar who studied at St John's College (circa 1972–1976). He held posts at Yale University (circa 1985–1987) and served as Director at Bard College circa 1987.

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned a PhD from Columbia University (attested 1983) under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, also studying under Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Kapferer (born 1940) studied at the Universities of Sydney and Manchester. A religious studies scholar, he held positions at the University of Adelaide, University of Gothenburg, University College London, James Cook University, and the University of Bergen (circa 1999–2015).

Bruce Lincoln (born 1948) earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. A scholar of religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history, he taught at the University of Minnesota (1976–1994) and the University of Chicago.
Bruce M. Knauft (born 1954) studied at the University of Michigan from circa 1976 to 1983. He served at Emory University from circa 1985 to 2020 as the Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology.

Bruce M. Sullivan (born 1951) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago in 1984. He was Professor Emeritus at Northern Arizona University.

Bruce Matthews (born 1941) is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who did graduate work at McMaster University. He served as a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon (1972–1974) and became Professor of Comparative Religion at Acadia University.

Bruce McCoy Owens is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1988) and has served as an associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens (1935–2023) studied under Colette Caillat in Indology and archaeology. He held posts at the EFEO, KU Leuven, the French Institute of Pondicherry as Indology section director, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University as Professor of Ancient History and Archaeology.
Bruno Galasek specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich (1862–1939) studied under Franz Kielhorn and earned degrees at Göttingen and Breslau. An Indology and linguistics scholar, he held posts at Heidelberg University and the University of Breslau, serving as Ordentlicher Professor für Indologie from 1921 to 1928.

Bruno Lindner (1853–1930) was an Indology, Iranian studies, and linguistics scholar educated at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Jena under teachers including Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Windisch. From 1878 to 1919, he served as Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig.

Bruno Meissner (1868–1947), a historian and archaeologist, studied at the universities of Leipzig and Strasbourg. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (circa 1904–1920) and Frederick William / Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1920–1936).

Bruno Petzold (1873–1949) studied at Leipzig and Berlin, later studying under Daito Shimaji and Shinsho Hanayama. A Buddhist and Japanese studies scholar, he taught German and Latin at the First Higher School (1917–1943) and taught at Chuo and Rissho universities.

Bruno Schindler (1882–1964) was a Sinologist who completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady. He founded Asia Major in 1923 and served as Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries from circa 1939 to 1964.
